items.title: David Sullivan steps down at West Ham to fight claims about private life
items.summary: Joint-chair and director of relegated club to tackle ‘false allegations’ ‘I am absolutely not the person the media has decided to paint me as’ David Sullivan has announced his resignation as a joint-chair and director of West Ham with immediate effect in a statement. Sullivan and his legal representatives published his intention to stand down on the club’s website on Saturday “for the benefit of transparency”. It read: “I have recently become aware that factually incorrect and entirely false, decades-old allegations concerning my personal life are due to be broadcast and published. Continue reading...

items.title: Italiaanse media: 'Terugkeer Stankovic bij Inter mogelijk van zeer korte duur'
items.summary: Internazionale heeft Aleksandar Stankovic terug naar Milaan gehaald. Echter, het is nog maar de vraag of de zoon van Inter-legende Dejan Stankovic daadwerkelijk minuten voor de Serie A-kampioen gaat maken. Italiaanse media vermoeden dat Stankovic komende zomer voor een flink bedrag meteen doorverkocht gaat worden.

items.title: Iraola heeft respect voor Slot en kijkt uit naar Champions League met Liverpool
items.summary: Andoni Iraola kijkt uit naar zijn debuut als manager van Liverpool, maar vooral naar de Champions League. Als speler speelde hij maar drie wedstrijden op het miljardenbal, waardoor de Spanjaard niet kan wachten om het tegen de beste teams van Europa op te nemen. Op de clubwebsite gaf Iraola ook aan veel respect voor zijn voorganger Arne Slot te hebben.

items.title: Iran slams US ‘discriminatory treatment’ over World Cup visa refusals
items.summary: Backroom staff denied entry visas for US, claims post on X Team have moved training base from Arizona to Mexico Iran has slammed World Cup co-hosts the United States over what it called “discriminatory treatment” by not granting visas for some members of the Iranian national team’s delegation to attend the tournament. “Why do you not say that visas were denied to a large portion of the managerial and executive staff, technical advisers, and others who are an integral part of any national football team?” the Iranian embassy in Turkey said in a post on X, referring to an earlier announcement by the US envoy Tom Barrack that visas had been granted to players. Continue reading...

items.title: Fifa backtracks on plastic water bottles ban at World Cup after fury from fans
items.summary: Fans will now be allowed one sealed bottle at matches Keir Starmer among critics of previous U-turn on policy Fifa has again amended its water bottle policy for the World Cup in North America, allowing fans to bring in one sealed, disposable 20-ounce (590ml) bottle into stadiums. Ticket holders had previously been permitted an empty, transparent and reusable bottle up to one litre but an update earlier this week confirmed reusable bottles were no longer permitted. Continue reading...
